status_note: active; v10.0.0 (Puppeteer 25, axe-core ~4.13, @pa11y/html_codesniffer 2.6 fork); sibling pa11y/pa11y-ci (LGPL-3.0, 633 stars, pushed 2026-09-13) provides sitemap/URL-list batch runs
core_problem: A Puppeteer-driven CLI and Node API that loads a URL, optionally performs a scripted list of pre-test actions, injects one or more in-page accessibility engines (HTML_CodeSniffer by default, axe optional), and normalizes their output into a single flat issue list with error/warning/notice levels, a threshold and exit code for CI.
architecture: lib/pa11y.js orchestrates a fixed sequence: option.parseArguments (defaults: standard WCAG2AA, runners ['htmlcs'], timeout 60000, viewport 1280x1024, includeNotices/includeWarnings false, levelCapWhenNeedsReview 'error', wait 0) -> setBrowser (puppeteer.launch(chromeLaunchConfig) or a caller-supplied browser/page) -> setPage (viewport, userAgent, console forwarding) -> interceptRequests (only if headers/method/postData) -> gotoUrl (waitUntil networkidle2, or ignoreUrl to audit an already-navigated page) -> runActionsList -> injectRunners (lib/runner.js + each runner's scripts via page.evaluate) -> wait -> runPa11yWithOptions -> saveScreenCapture. lib/runner.js is the in-page aggregator exposed as window.__pa11y: runs each named runner, filters issues by rootElement / hideElements / ignore (codes or types), and maps each to {code, type error|warning|notice, typeCode 1|2|3, message, context (outerHTML truncated to 250 chars, innerHTML to 31), selector (id-anchored 'tag:nth-child' path), runner, runnerExtras}. Runners are plugins {scripts: [paths injected], run(options, pa11y), supports: semver}: lib/runners/htmlcs.js calls HTMLCS.process(standard, document) with standard WCAG2A|WCAG2AA|WCAG2AAA and optional extra sniff 'rules', mapping HTMLCS type 1/2/3 to error/warning/notice; lib/runners/axe.js calls axe.run(rootElement||document, {runOnly: {type:'tags', values:['wcag2a','wcag21a', +'wcag2aa','wcag21aa' unless WCAG2A, 'best-practice']}, rules: enable/disable map derived from pa11y rules/ignore}) and maps impact critical|serious -> error, moderate -> warning, minor -> notice; crucially it emits axe 'incomplete' results as issues with runnerExtras.needsFurtherReview = true, capped to levelCapWhenNeedsReview. lib/action.js is a regex-matched DSL run before testing: 'navigate to <url>', 'click element <sel>', 'set field <sel> to <val>', 'clear field', 'check|uncheck field', 'screen capture <file>', 'wait for url|path|fragment|host to (not) be <x>', 'wait for element <sel> to be added|removed|visible|hidden', 'wait for element <sel> to emit <event>'. Reporters (lib/reporters): cli, csv, tsv, json, html (mustache template). CLI (bin/pa11y.js): --runner, --standard, --threshold N (exit 2 if issues > N), --level, --level-cap-when-needs-review, --ignore, --add-rule, --root-element, --hide-elements, --config JSON. pa11y-ci: lib/pa11y-ci.js runs an async queue (concurrency default 1, useIncognitoBrowserContext true) over 'urls' (each a string or {url, ...overrides, threshold}) or a --sitemap (recurses sitemapindex, --sitemap-find/--sitemap-replace to rewrite hosts, --sitemap-exclude regex), cycles reporters through beforeAll/begin/results/error/afterAll, and exits 2 when errors >= threshold.
core_innovation: Runner abstraction that normalizes heterogeneous a11y engines into one issue schema, plus a plain-English pre-test action DSL so page state can be set up without writing browser code.
strengths: Dual engines: HTML_CodeSniffer catches some WCAG techniques axe does not express (and WCAG2AAA sniffs), giving a cheap second opinion on the same DOM.

Needs-review policy is explicit: axe incomplete results are surfaced as issues (needsFurtherReview true) and their level is capped by levelCapWhenNeedsReview, so 'unknown' is never silently dropped - the same fail-closed posture our gate wants.
Issue schema is tiny and stable (code/type/message/context/selector/runner) and identical across engines; trivially mapped into a GateReport.
Action DSL is human-readable and validatable (pa11y.isValidAction), suitable for authoring per-archetype pre-conditions in YAML.
pa11y-ci provides sitemap-driven batch runs with per-URL threshold overrides and a minimal reporter lifecycle contract.
Accepts an external Puppeteer browser/page (browser + page + ignoreUrl), so it can run on a page another script already navigated.
weaknesses: LGPL-3.0-only: acceptable for unmodified use as a CLI or npm dependency in a closed SaaS (LGPL section 4 applies to combined works; dynamic linking/consumption via npm is customary), but any modification to pa11y's own source must be published, and some enterprise clients flag LGPL in dependency audits. Nothing here is worth that friction.
Puppeteer, not Playwright: a second browser driver and Chrome download in our stack, with its own lifecycle, for a job Playwright + @axe-core/playwright already does.

HTML_CodeSniffer is a legacy engine (pa11y's own fork, minor updates), noisy notices, and its WCAG 2.1 mapping is partial; its unique value versus axe is small for modern semantic HTML that our section library controls.

Flattens axe's rich result: any/all/none check data, relatedNodes, tags and helpUrl are lost or squashed into message text; impact->level mapping discards 'incomplete' as a distinct status (only a boolean in runnerExtras).
Selector generation (id-anchored nth-child path) is weaker than axe's own target arrays and does not traverse iframes or shadow DOM.
Per-page tool; pa11y-ci has no route sampling, no dedupe, no cross-page checks, and threshold is a plain count rather than severity-weighted.
Runs with a desktop 1280x1024 viewport by default; no built-in multi-viewport runs, no throttling, no performance or SEO checks.
patterns_to_steal: Needs-review cap (levelCapWhenNeedsReview) -> qa_gate: policy knob that decides whether axe 'incomplete' nodes fail, warn or inform, defaulting to fail (error) for launch.

Action DSL grammar ('click element X', 'wait for element X to be visible', 'set field X to Y') -> qa_gate: author per page-archetype pre-test steps (open mobile nav, submit contact form, dismiss cookie banner) in YAML and compile them to Playwright calls; validate at load time like pa11y.isValidAction.
Runner plugin contract {scripts, run, supports} -> qa_gate: our in-page checks (placeholder scan, h1 count, generic link text) as runners that share the axe/HTMLCS injection path and result schema.
Uniform issue row {code, type, message, context, selector, runner} -> GateReport row baseline; add status (fail|warn|needs_review|pass|n/a), impact, tags, target[] and screenshot ref on top.
pa11y-ci urls entry as string | {url, overrides, threshold} -> qa_gate config: per-page overrides for pages with legitimately different rules (legal pages, thank-you page).
patterns_to_avoid: Adding pa11y as a dependency -> duplicates Playwright with Puppeteer, drags in LGPL, and loses axe result fidelity; run @axe-core/playwright directly.
HTML_CodeSniffer as a gate engine -> unmaintained mapping and noisy notices would create non-actionable failures; at most run it informative-only in research to spot gaps in our section library.
Count-based threshold ('permit N issues') -> we gate on severity classes and specific check ids, never on totals; a single critical is a fail, ten minors are warnings.
Default desktop-only viewport -> our checks must run at mobile 412x823 (Lighthouse's Moto G emulation) and desktop 1350x940 so target-size and contrast are evaluated where users see them.
reusable_patterns: NeedsReviewSeverityCap: undecidable machine results are surfaced as issues with a configurable maximum severity, defaulting to fail-closed.
PlainEnglishActionDSL: regex-matched imperative sentences compiled to browser actions, validated before the run.
EngineRunnerPlugin: {scripts, run(options), supports} lets multiple in-page engines share injection, filtering and output schema.
PerUrlThresholdOverride: batch config where each URL can override defaults and its own pass threshold.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a dependency; Adapt two small patterns. Given Playwright + @axe-core/playwright are already in the stack, pa11y is redundant: its axe runner is a thin wrapper that loses data, and HTML_CodeSniffer adds little for semantic HTML we author ourselves. Take (1) the needs-review severity cap as a gate policy setting and (2) the action-sentence DSL for authoring pre-test steps per archetype in YAML, implemented over Playwright. Do not vendor its code (LGPL); the patterns are trivial to re-implement (~100 lines).

lib/runners/axe.js (runOnly tags wcag2a/wcag21a/wcag2aa/wcag21aa/best-practice; impact->level map critical/serious=error moderate=warning minor=notice; incomplete emitted with needsFurtherReview=true and capped by levelCapWhenNeedsReview; supports '^10.0.0')

lib/action.js (action regexes: navigate-url, click-element, set-field-value, clear-field-value, check-field, screen-capture, wait-for-url, wait-for-element-state, wait-for-element-event)
lib/option.js (parseArguments/defaultOptions: notices/warnings pushed onto ignore unless included; sanitizeUrl file:// handling)
